body.text: Śaraṇagamanadeśanā
body.translated_text: <s>Śaraṇagamanadeśanā</s> (Teaching on Going for Refuge)

body.text: namo ratnatrayāya
body.translated_text: Homage to the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>)!

children.translated_text: I bow to him who destroys all suffering of the three lower realms (<s>tryapāya</s>) and five types of birth (<s>pañcayoni</s>),
and who is the giver of the happiness of welfare (<s>śreyas</s>) and prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>). (1)

body.text: atra śaraṇagamanamabhidhāsye / samāsataḥ /

children.translated_text: The basis (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), abiding (<s>sthiti</s>), intention (<s>cintā</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), measure (<s>māna</s>),
method (<s>naya</s>), training (<s>śikṣā</s>), etymology (<s>nirukti</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), analogy (<s>upamya</s>), and divisions (<s>vibhakti</s>),
disadvantages (<s>ādīnava</s>), meaning (<s>artha</s>), and praises (<s>śaṃsā</s>) — these fifteen [topics] are taught in order. (2)

body.translated_text: Here I shall explain going for refuge (<s>śaraṇagamana</s>), in brief.

body.text: tatra adhiṣṭhānapudgalastu dvividhaḥ- mahāyānagotrīyo hīnayānagotrīyaśca / sthitirdvividhā- mahā-hīna-yānabhedataḥ / tatraivaṃ hi tāvad mahāyānaśāstreṣu ratnatrayam- tathatāratnatrayam, abhisamayaratnatrayaṃ, sammukhasthaṃ ca ratnatrayam /
body.translated_text: Among these, the basis-person (<s>adhiṣṭhānapudgala</s>) is of two kinds: one belonging to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> lineage (<s>gotra</s>) and one belonging to the <s>Hīnayāna</s> lineage. The abiding is twofold, by the distinction of <s>Mahāyāna</s> and <s>Hīnayāna</s>. Here, in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> treatises, the Three Jewels [are threefold]: the Three Jewels of Suchness (<s>tathatāratnatraya</s>), the Three Jewels of Clear Realization (<s>abhisamayaratnatraya</s>), and the Three Jewels Present Before One (<s>sammukhasthaṃ ratnatraya</s>).

body.text: taccaivam- jñeyāviparyastajñānam, nirvikalpādvayajñānam, dharmadhātvavasthitatvaṃ ca / tadeva viśuddha-dharmadhātuprajñāpāramitā, samāhitāvasthāyāṃ gaganatalavat samastadharmasākṣātkāriṇyāṃ mahābhūmau avasthitāḥ bodhisattvāśca (tathatāratnatrayam) /
body.translated_text: And that is thus: knowledge not inverted regarding the knowable (<s>jñeyāviparyastajñāna</s>), non-conceptual non-dual knowledge (<s>nirvikalpādvayajñāna</s>), and abiding in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (dharma-realm). That itself is the pure <s>dharmadhātu</s>-<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom); and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established on the great stages (<s>mahābhūmi</s>), who in the state of meditative equipoise directly perceive all <s>dharmas</s> like the surface of the sky — [these constitute] the Three Jewels of Suchness (<s>tathatāratnatraya</s>).

body.text: atha caivaṃ- dvividho rupakāyaḥ , santānāvasthitāścatuḥsatya-saptatriṃśadbodhipākṣikadharma-bhūmi-pāramitādayo dharmāḥ, prayogamārgīyāśca bodhisattvāḥ /
body.translated_text: And also thus: the twofold <s>rūpakāya</s> (form-body), the <s>dharmas</s> abiding in the [mind-]continuum such as the Four Truths (<s>catuḥsatya</s>), the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>saptatriṃśadbodhipākṣikadharma</s>), the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>), the perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), and so forth; and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> on the Path of Application (<s>prayogamārga</s>).

body.text: punaścaivam- citrāṅkitatotkīrṇaniṣiktamṛṇmayādi (buddhapratimādi) - navāṅgapravacanamayapothīpustakādi, saṃbhāramārgīyāśca bodhisatvāḥ / hīnayānaśāstraṃ tāvat-
body.translated_text: And furthermore thus: painted, engraved, cast, clay-made, and other [<s>Buddha</s> images], books and manuscripts consisting of the nine divisions of the teaching (<s>navāṅgapravacana</s>); and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> on the Path of Accumulation (<s>saṃbhāramārga</s>). As for the <s>Hīnayāna</s> treatise —

body.text:
buddhasaṃghakarāndharmān aśaikṣānubhayāṃśca saḥ /
nirvāṇaṃ ceti śaraṇaṃ yo yāti śaraṇatrayam // 3 // iti /
tatra āśayo mahāyānināntu aśeṣasattvārthacintanam / itarasya ca ātmārthameva cintanam /
body.translated_text: 'He who goes for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the <s>dharmas</s> of those beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), both [categories], and <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — that is the threefold refuge.' (3) Here, the intention of the <s>Mahāyānins</s> is the contemplation of the welfare of all beings without exception; and of the other [<s>Hīnayānins</s>], the contemplation is only for one's own benefit.

body.text: tatra avadhirmahāyānināntu bodhimaṇḍaparyantam / itarasya tu yāvajjīvanaṃ pratijñā /
body.translated_text: The limit (<s>avadhi</s>) for the <s>Mahāyānins</s> is until the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>); for the other, the vow is for as long as one lives.

body.text:
tatra svabhāvo hrī-apatrapāyuktatā avijñaptpādaśca /
tatra mānaṃ tu svīkaraṇam, śaraṇakaraṇaṃ vijñaptyutpādaśca /
tatra nayastu śaraṇagamanavidhiḥ / sa ca guroravagantavyaḥ /
tatra śikṣā sādhāraṇī asādhāraṇī ca gurupādebhyo jñeyā /
tatra niruktistu dāsabhāvaḥ taditarasvāminamananviṣya śaraṇagamanam /
body.translated_text: The own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is the state of being endowed with shame (<s>hrī</s>) and moral dread (<s>apatrapā</s>), and the non-manifest [action] (<s>avijñapti</s>). The acceptance (<s>māna</s>) is the taking upon oneself, the undertaking of refuge, and the arising of manifest [action] (<s>vijñapti</s>). The method (<s>naya</s>) is the procedure for going for refuge; and that should be learned from the <s>guru</s> (teacher). The training (<s>śikṣā</s>), both common (<s>sādhāraṇī</s>) and uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇī</s>), should be known from the teacher. The etymology (<s>nirukti</s>): servitude (<s>dāsabhāva</s>) — going for refuge without seeking any other master.

body.text: tatra kāritraṃ tu bodhicittamahāvṛkṣotpādasya mūlatvam, mokṣamahānagarasya praveśadvāratvam, upavāsādisarvasaṃvarāṇām āśrayatvam /
body.translated_text: The function (<s>kāritra</s>) is: being the root for the arising of the great tree of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind), being the entrance-gate to the great city of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), and being the basis for all vows (<s>saṃvaras</s>) such as the fasting observance (<s>upavāsa</s>).

body.text: tatraupamyaṃ tāvad rājñaḥ mantriṇo vā prajāgaṇasya tadvacanānatikramaṇam, tadārādhanamiva ca /
body.translated_text: The analogy (<s>upamya</s>) is like the populace not transgressing the words of the king or the minister, and like serving them.

body.text: tatra bhedastu sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇatvena viśiṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: The division (<s>bheda</s>) is distinguished by being common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) and uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>).

body.text: tatra ādīnavau dvau / śaraṇacyutirajñānaṃ vā / cyavanaṃ cyutirvā yathā candrakīrtipādānām-
body.translated_text: The disadvantages (<s>ādīnava</s>) are two: falling away from refuge (<s>śaraṇacyuti</s>), or ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>). Falling away or lapsing, as stated by the venerable <s>Candrakīrti</s> —

body.text:
gṛhītvā sadadhiṣṭhānaṃ punarhīnasamāśraye /
cyutipakṣāśrayatvāt so yāti sajjanahāsyatām // 4 // ityuktirnidarśanamātram /
body.translated_text: 'Having taken the excellent basis, if one then relies on an inferior [refuge], because of being on the side of lapsing, one becomes an object of ridicule among good people.' (4) This statement is merely an illustration.

body.text: tatrārthastu yathoktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: The meaning [of refuge] is as stated by the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) —

children.translated_text: 'Many go for refuge to mountains and forests,
to gardens, trees, and shrines — people who are free from [immediate] fear. (5)
But this is not the best refuge, this is not the supreme refuge;
by coming to this refuge, one is not freed from all suffering. (6)

children.text: yastu buddhaṃ ca dharma ca saṃghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: But one who has gone for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>,
when one sees with wisdom the Four Noble Truths (<s>catvāri āryasatyāni</s>) — (7)
suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), the origin of suffering (<s>duḥkhasamutpāda</s>), the transcendence of suffering,
and the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgikamārga</s>) leading to the peace of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — (8)

body.text:
etaddhi śaraṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ etaccharaṇamuttamam /
etaccharaṇamāgamya sarvaduḥkhāt pramucyate // 9 // iti /
body.translated_text: this indeed is the best refuge, this is the supreme refuge; by coming to this refuge, one is freed from all suffering.' (9)

body.text: śaraṇagamamārthaḥ tādṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Such is the meaning of going for refuge.

body.text: tatrānuśaṃsāstimnaḥ / hetukālānuśaṃsā mārgakālānuśaṃsā phalakālānuśaṃsā ca / hetukālā ehikī āmuṣmikī ca / ehikānuśaṃsā aṣṭamahābhayamokṣaḥ, anantarāyaḥ, śāsanapriyadevasāhāyyam, maraṇakāle ca cittaharṣādi / āmuṣmikī tu saṃsāradurgati-duḥkhebhya uddharaṇam, nirvāṇābhyudayasukhapradattvañca / mārgānuśaṃsā tu catu-(rārya-)satyāryāṣṭāṅgikamārga-saptabodhyaṅgādiyojanam / phalānusaṃsā dvividhanirvāṇasya trikāyasya ca prāptiḥ /
body.translated_text: Regarding this, the benefits are threefold: the benefits at the time of the cause, the benefits at the time of the path, and the benefits at the time of the fruit. The benefits at the time of the cause are of two kinds: pertaining to this life and pertaining to the next. The benefits pertaining to this life are: liberation from the eight great fears, absence of obstacles, the assistance of the gods who are devoted to the teaching, and joy of mind at the time of death, and so forth. The benefits pertaining to the next life are: deliverance from the sufferings of the evil destinies in <s>saṃsāra</s>, and the bestowal of the happiness of <s>nirvāṇa</s> and worldly prosperity. The benefits at the time of the path are: the application of the Four Noble Truths (<s>catvāry āryasatyāni</s>), the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgikamārga</s>), the Seven Factors of Awakening (<s>saptabodhyaṅga</s>), and so forth. The benefits at the time of the fruit are: the attainment of the twofold <s>nirvāṇa</s> and of the Three Bodies (<s>trikāya</s>).

body.text: idaṃ hi saṃkṣiptam, vistaraṃ tu guruśāstrabhyo jñeyam /
body.translated_text: This has been stated in brief; the details should be learned from the <s>guru</s>'s teachings (<s>śāstra</s>).

body.text: śaraṇagamanadeśanā-nāma gurubodhisattva-dīpaṅkara-śrījñānaviracitā samāptā //
body.translated_text: The <s>Śaraṇagamanadeśanā</s> (Instruction on Taking Refuge), composed by the <s>guru</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara Śrījñāna</s>, is complete.
